newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross presses Zaire rebels for refugee access.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross presses Zaire rebels for refugee access.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross joined calls by other aid agencies and the United Nations on Thursday for rebels in east Zaire to provide access to thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees on the run.
The Swiss-run ICRC said in a statement the displaced Rwandans were in a disastrous state and that any new forced movement could lead to the deaths of thousands of refugees.

"With the arrival of heavy rains in areas with dense vegetation, the scale of needs has become alarming. It is no longer a matter of feeding the hungry but of coping with serious medical emergencies," the Geneva-based agency said.
Aid officials said Tutsi-dominated rebels led by Laurent Kabila had failed so far to keep promises of access to refugees.

The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR is waiting for Kabila's consent to allow relief workers to get through the rebel-held city of Kisangani to reach some 80,000 refugees situated some 16 to 25 miles (26 to 40 km) south of the city.
A UNHCR spokeswoman said Kabila's permission was also needed to start an airlift of the weakest refugees back to Rwanda.
